title: The Last Witness
premise: Estate lawyer Jude Sterling is hired by a dying woman, Marisol Vane, to draft a will for a man who is still alive — and to prove his murder hasn't happened yet. When the man dies exactly as Marisol predicted, Jude realizes the killer is someone with access to her own firm's confidential files. As she investigates outside the law with help from a disgraced former detective and a runaway teen witness, she discovers Marisol orchestrated everything to force justice for a cold case the town buried a decade ago. In the end, Jude must choose between protecting her found family and turning over the evidence that will convict the killer — and herself.
about_author: Lena Eastwick spent fifteen years in small-town courtrooms before trading legal pads for fiction. She writes mysteries about people who know exactly where the bodies are filed.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Jude Sterling's POV. A frail Marisol Vane pays double to have Jude draft a will for Edmund Hale — dated three days before his predicted murder. Jude assumes senility until Marisol recites details of Hale's death that haven't happened. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into dread as Jude pockets an advance she suddenly doesn't want.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Three days later, Hale is dead exactly as described. Jude combs her firm's decade of files and finds Hale's name redacted across six unrelated estates — all tied to a 2015 drowning ruled accidental. Beat: guilt; she has been the town's filing cabinet for its sins without ever reading them.

chapters.title: The Detective Who Quit
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: ex-detective Ray Okonkwo, drunk and retired after botching the 2015 case, is dragged back when Jude shows him the will. He recognizes the drowning detail only the real killer would know. Beat: reluctant alliance, two people who each believe they failed the same victim.

chapters.title: Witness Number Four
chapters.summary: Teen runaway Wren's POV. Wren saw something the night Hale died and lifted Marisol's wallet — inside, a photo of the 2015 victim and a list of five names, four crossed out. She seeks out Jude instead of selling it. Beat: wary connection; Wren becomes the daughter-shaped hole in Jude's life.

chapters.title: Five Names
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The list maps to the five people present at the 2015 drowning. Two are already dead by 'accident.' The third is Jude's senior partner, who warns her off with chilling gentleness. Beat: betrayal — the conspiracy ran through her own office, and her mentor may be next on the list or on it as author.

chapters.title: What Marisol Knew
chapters.summary: Ray's POV. Ray tracks Marisol's decade of quiet investigation — letters, bribes refused, a daughter lost in 2015. But Marisol has vanished from her hospice bed. Beat: grief and awe; Marisol isn't a client, she's an architect, and they're building inside her blueprint.

chapters.title: The Third Name
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren tails the third living name, Councilman Brandt, and photographs him burning documents — then realizes someone is tailing her. A narrow escape leaves her injured and hiding at Jude's. Beat: fear hardening into resolve; the found family stops being metaphor and starts sharing one roof.

chapters.title: Confession, Drafted
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude finds Marisol hiding in the firm's archive room, dying, and takes her final statement — a full confession not of murder but of manipulation: she leaked the files to bait the killer into finishing what the law wouldn't touch. Beat: moral vertigo; every clue was planted, including their hope.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ray and Jude's alternating POV. At Hale's estate reading, Jude springs the trap: reads the impossible will aloud, forcing the killer — the firm's silent co-founder — to contest a document that proves he knew the murder schedule. Ray records his outburst; Wren's photos seal it. Beat: triumphant tension snapping into violence and near-tragedy.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Jude's POV, epilogue-like. The killer is charged; Jude surrenders her role in Marisol's scheme and accepts suspension, choosing accountability over the alphabetized safety of silence. She, Ray, and Wren scatter Marisol's ashes where the truth finally surfaced. Beat: bittersweet peace — justice arrived outside the law, and love stayed despite duty.
